capability.summary: Fix two engine-timing bugs that combined to produce audible sloppiness and progressive degradation across a session: (1) Tone.js was running on its own AudioContext while sample playback used the app's AudioContext, so every src.start(time) was scheduled ~22s in the past — measured min delta when - ctxTime = -22.547s on main. After Tone.setContext(audioCtx), measured min delta = +0.043s (Tone's normal lookahead). (2) Each ADSR-enabled trigger leaked a GainNode into the audio graph because the envelope was never disconnected after the source ended — measured 4 alive after one play cycle, 12 after three cycles. After adding source.addEventListener('ended', () => env.disconnect()) the count stays at 0 across cycles.

controls.description: After initAudio(), main.ts calls Tone.setContext(getAudioContext()) so the Tone.Transport clock runs on the same AudioContext that owns all sample playback nodes. Every src.start(time) lands at or after the context's currentTime.
controls.test: e2e: instrument createBufferSource.start to capture (when, ctxTime); after one play, assert no captured delta is negative and min delta >= 0.

controls.description: applyEnvelope registers an 'ended' listener on the source that disconnects the env GainNode. Over multiple play/stop cycles the alive-GainNode count stays bounded.
controls.test: e2e: instrument createGain + disconnect to track alive count; after 3 play/stop cycles with ADSR enabled, alive count equals the pre-cycle baseline.
